crypto-lab-lfsr-forge.note: Read the complete merged README, source, tests, learner interface and visible limitations at this exact main commit. The existing binary Fibonacci LFSR, Berlekamp-Massey, Geffe-correlation and eSTREAM-vector-checked Trivium lessons remain, and the Trivium implementation anchors directly at the state-advance function rather than at a panel mount. The zero-round recovery builds 66 public equations over 80 key bits, exhausts the remaining 14-bit space, rechecks every candidate against the complete 1,024-bit observation and compares a unique candidate with the hidden key separately; the specified 1,152-round route rejects this model, and the lesson does not claim a cube attack against full Trivium. The Boolean panel exhaustively analyzes an editable four-input truth table: exact ANF and degree, all 16 Walsh coefficients, balance, nonlinearity, every fixed-subset distribution, correlation immunity, resiliency and 4,094 candidate-side checks over all 2,047 nonzero degree-at-most-two polynomials. Its deterministic counterexamples fit parity with Berlekamp-Massey, scan all 105 R1/R2 state pairs against an order-one-resilient function and scan all 127 R4 states against an algebraic-immunity-two function; worker inputs contain only copied output and the fixed public profile, while hidden-state comparisons stay in the controller. The eighth panel executes a cube attack on its own explicit three-secret/four-public degree-four GF(2) toy oracle. Preprocessing exhausts four two-variable cube faces over all eight teaching keys, computes 128 raw evaluations covering 72 distinct secret/public-row pairs and derives each superpoly by Möbius transform. C12, C13 and C24 are affine maxterms whose rank-three system filters 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 to key 110 from sums 111; C34 is a valid cube with the quadratic superpoly k1k2 ⊕ k3, is not a maxterm, and is excluded only from this bounded affine solve. The candidate is frozen before four disjoint held-out public rows; their 1011 fingerprint is injective over the eight teaching keys and precedes a separate controller comparison. Dropping C24 leaves 001 and 110, while flipping C13 recovers wrong candidate 000 before held-outs reject it. Online work is 12 raw cube-vertex evaluations plus four held-outs, 16 raw evaluations across 12 distinct public rows. The panel executes no Trivium state or round and makes no attack or cost claim against full Trivium; the cited paper treats only 672-, 735- and 767-round reduced variants. Its source-visible publication caveat says direct evaluation of ePrint 2008/385's printed introductory polynomial adds a constant 1 to the stated v3 = 0 face sum, so the lab uses its own independently checkable oracle and does not call that an official erratum. The ninth panel implements the reverse-engineered historical BGW A5/1 definition, not a public modern standard: distinct 19/22/23-bit registers, least-significant-bit-first Kc and COUNT loading, 100 output-disabled majority clocks and clock-before-output generation. Independently transcribed setup code derives the post-key, post-COUNT and post-100 checkpoint states, then matches the two published consecutive 114-bit bursts. Its separate bounded adaptation discloses an extraordinary 52 exact bits of one post-100 state, enumerates the remaining 4,096 completions and filters candidate 1425 with 32 aligned known-keystream bits before 32 disjoint held-out bits and a separate controller-state comparison. Sixteen bits leave 11 candidates, regular clocking leaves none after two observations, and flipping observation 29 selects wrong candidate 1409 before 11 held-out mismatches reject it. The worker receives only the masked 52-bit disclosure, copied observations, clock model and run identifier; it receives no full hidden state or Kc. The exercise is not a published A5/1 attack, does not recover Kc and does not model modern cellular encryption. The merged gates cover 47 unit tests, 23 browser tests, all nine panels at desktop/380px plus the 320px extension, and 33 clean-baseline mutations. Walsh probabilities and fixed-subset independence assume independent uniform table inputs; LFSR agreement is measured separately, both state scans are bounded toy searches, nonlinear-superpoly techniques remain out of scope, and algebraic immunity does not exclude every fast algebraic relation. The literal Brute force scanner hit appears only in the independent unit-test oracle. Panel 09 separately exhausts 2^12 state completions under disclosure of 52 exact post-100 state bits; the catalog records that narrowly as bounded state completion, not as a generic brute-force attack or A5/1/Kc attack. Known plaintext/ciphertext remains prose explaining how an external XOR-stream setting could reveal the already-supplied keystream and is not an attack workflow executed by this lab. Shamir names a cube-attack coauthor, while Pairing and RC4 are stale or lexical false references, so none of those three belongs in the algorithm reference list. BCH, ChaCha20, SHA-256, SNOW 3G and ZUC remain comparison or evidence context rather than implemented primitives.
